Subject: Planned maintenance — EU-WEST3 rolling node swap & kernel hardening (Nov 29)

Hello Samantha and Acme infra team,

We have a scheduled maintenance window on Sunday, Nov 29 for the EU-WEST3 region to perform a rolling node swap and kernel microcode hardening across inference fleets. This is a controlled maintenance intended to reduce a class of rare kernel-initiated OOM/eviction events observed during long-running KV-heavy chat sessions.

Window: 2026-11-29 01:00 — 05:00 UTC (4 hours)
Impact: Rolling restarts per host; typical per-request latency should be unaffected. For a small fraction of long-running sessions (approx 0.5%) you may see a single reconnect/failover. No model state/data will be lost — KV caches are preserved and warmed on failover where possible.

Mitigations and fallbacks:
- Traffic will be routed away from draining hosts using our smart routing policy and automatic fallback to adjacent EU zones.
- Canary batch will run first on a subset of hosts with monitoring hooks.
- Live migrations for active reserved sessions will be attempted; where unavailable, in-flight requests will be retried.

Action for customers: No immediate action required. If you have pinned model instances in Dedicated or Private deployments, please reply with the hostnames so we can coordinate a pause.

Attachments: maintenance-runbook-euw3.pdf (runbook), euw3-window.ics (calendar block)
Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/REDACTED-runbooks-euw3

I'll post live updates to this thread during the window. If you need an SLA exception or extended runway, please tell us before 2026-11-29 00:00 UTC.

Thanks,
Priyom Das

Hi Samantha — thanks for the quick note. Short answers: 

1) Reserved/Dedicated sessions: we will attempt live migration for those instances. For Dedicated pools that are explicitly pinned to hosts (rare), we have a coordinated pause option — please send the hostnames (ex: dedicated-us-euw3-01) and we'll exclude them from the first canary and schedule a manual handoff during a second window.

2) SLA credits: our standard maintenance policy (linked in the runbook) does not automatically issue credits for planned rolling maintenance when we provide notice.
